name: Erdheim-Chester Disease

criteria.description: Histological confirmation: foamy histiocytes (lipid-laden macrophages) positive for CD68 and CD163, negative for CD1a and langerin
Bilateral symmetric osteosclerosis of long bone diaphyses/metaphyses on imaging
BRAF V600E mutation or other MAPK pathway mutation in lesional tissue
Characteristic perinephric/periaortic soft tissue infiltration ('coated aorta' or 'hairy kidney')

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation with appropriate immunophenotype (CD68+, CD1a-) combined with compatible clinical and radiographic features. BRAF testing should be performed in all cases.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Classified as a neoplastic histiocytic disorder (WHO 2016 revision). BRAF V600E mutation present in ~55-70% of cases. May overlap with LCH ('mixed histiocytosis').

pathognomonic.notes: Most common presenting symptom; lower extremities, especially knees

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral symmetric osteosclerosis of long bone diaphyses on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Virtually pathognomonic when present; symmetric cortical thickening on X-ray/CT

rare.notes: Can cause pericardial tamponade; pseudotumor of right atrium

laboratory: BRAF V600E mutation positive in 55-70% (blood or tissue)
Other MAPK pathway mutations (MAP2K1, KRAS, NRAS) in BRAF-wild-type cases
Mild anemia, elevated LDH may be present
imaging: X-ray/CT: bilateral symmetric osteosclerotic lesions of long bone diaphyses (virtually diagnostic)
Tc-99m bone scan: symmetric increased uptake in long bones
CT abdomen: perinephric soft tissue ('hairy kidney'), circumferential periaortic sheathing ('coated aorta')
PET-CT: FDG-avid osseous and extraosseous lesions
MRI brain: thickened pituitary stalk, retro-orbital masses, parenchymal lesions
genetic: Other MAPK pathway: KRAS, NRAS, ARAF, PIK3CA
Not inherited; somatic mutations in myeloid precursors
other: Biopsy: foamy histiocytes, Touton giant cells, fibrosis
Immunohistochemistry: CD68+, CD163+, factor XIIIa+, CD1a-, langerin-
Targeted therapy with vemurafenib/cobimetinib for BRAF/MEK-mutated cases

distinguishingFeatures: LCH is CD1a+ and langerin+; ECD is CD1a-
LCH causes lytic bone lesions; ECD causes sclerotic lesions
LCH more common in children; ECD more common in adults
Idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis lacks bone involvement
IgG4-related disease may mimic but has elevated IgG4 and plasmacytic infiltrate

redFlags: CNS involvement (seizures, cognitive decline, cerebellar ataxia)
Bilateral ureteral obstruction with renal failure
references: Diamond EL, et al. Consensus guidelines for the diagnosis and clinical management of Erdheim-Chester disease. Blood. 2014;124(4):483-492.
Haroche J, et al. High prevalence of BRAF V600E mutations in Erdheim-Chester disease but not in other non-Langerhans cell histiocytoses. Blood. 2012;120(13):2700-2703.
Goyal G, et al. Erdheim-Chester disease: consensus recommendations for evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment in the molecular era. Blood. 2020;135(22):1929-1945.
